message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest, lightest, and most abundant element in the universe.  
Below is a concise overview of its key physical, chemical, and nuclear properties.

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Isotopes | Protium (^1H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (^2H, 0.02 %) – stable; Tritium (^3H) – radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV (73 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Physical Properties (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 g cm⁻³) |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Electrical conductivity | Poor (except when ionized) |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (≈0.61 cm² s⁻¹ at 25 °C) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms covalent bonds with many elements; reacts with halogens, oxygen, nitrogen, etc. |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (elemental) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HF) or base (H₂O) depending on context; forms hydrides (e.g., LiH, CaH₂) |
| | Combustion | Combines with O₂ → H₂O; releases ~286 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Reducing agent | Strong reducing agent (e.g., in the reduction of metal oxides) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Forms strong H‑bond networks in water, alcohols, amides, etc. |
| | Spectroscopic signatures | 1H NMR (δ ≈ 0 ppm for free H₂), IR (stretching ~ 3657 cm⁻¹ for OH), UV‑Vis (no d‑d transitions) |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.7928 µ_N (protium) |
| | Tritium decay | β⁻ decay to ^3He (β‑endpoint 18.6 keV) |
| **Applications & Uses** | Energy carrier | Fuel cell (electrochemical) and rocket propulsion (liquid/solid) |
| | Industrial processes | Haber–Bosch (NH₃ synthesis), Fischer–Tropsch (synthetic fuels), methanol production, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Materials science | Hydride formation (LiH, CaH₂), metal hydrides for storage |
| | Analytical chemistry | NMR (¹H), mass spectrometry (H₂⁺), spectroscopy (UV‑Vis, IR) |
| | Medicine & biology | Radiolabeling (tritium), MRI contrast agents (deuterated solvents) |
| | Environmental science | Greenhouse gas (water vapor), climate studies (H₂O isotopologues) |
| **Miscellaneous** | Abundance | ~75 % of baryonic mass in the universe; ~90 % of stars’ mass |
| | Specific energy | 142 MJ kg⁻¹ (≈33 kWh kg⁻¹) – highest among fuels |
| | Safety | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (1–4 % H₂ in air) |

---

### Quick Reference Summary

- **Atomic number:** 1  
- **Symbol:** H  
- **Average mass:** 1.008 u  
- **Isotopes:** ^1H (stable), ^2H (stable), ^3H (radioactive)  
- **Boiling point:** –252.87 °C (20.28 K)  
- **Melting point:** –259.16 °C (14 K)  
- **Density (STP):** 0.08988 g L⁻¹  
- **Electronegativity:** 2.20  
- **First ionization energy:** 13.598 eV  
- **Electron affinity:** 0.754 eV  
- **Bond dissociation energy (H–H):** 436 kJ mol⁻¹  
- **Combustion enthalpy:** –286 kJ mol⁻¹  
- **Specific energy (fuel):** 142 MJ kg⁻¹  

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any of these aspects!
